candidate_relations.reason: Neuralgic amyotrophy denotes the same brachial plexus/peripheral nerve inflammatory syndrome as Parsonage-Turner syndrome.

The anterior interosseous pattern explains the OK-sign and finger-flexion weakness, but EMG abnormalities also involve biceps, triceps, and deltoid, supporting broader Parsonage-Turner syndrome rather than an isolated entrapment syndrome.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Focal anterior interosseous motor syndrome rather than the full neuralgic amyotrophy diagnosis.

candidate_relations.reason: The clinical and EMG findings include anterior interosseous neuropathy, but additional proximal muscle involvement means this label does not capture the full Parsonage-Turner diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Anterior interosseous nerve involvement is a focal manifestation/component of the broader syndrome.
